Sam (Customer): hitting a pretty consistent issue where after a client-side reconnect the SSE stream sometimes emits a duplicate full generation. customer sees repeated paragraphs (billing duplicates). repro attached, low-volume prod traffic so it's not load-related.

Maya (CSE): thanks Sam — can you paste a minimal repro + SDK version? are the duplicates exact byte-for-byte repeats or slightly different? any sequence ids in the stream? :thinking:

Sam (Customer): exact repeats most of the time. here's a short curl repro hitting /v1/stream with a session token, reconnecting after drop. SDK is our in-house wrapper (not Redwood SDK).

Sam (Customer): ```bash
# initial connect, read a couple events then force-close socket to emulate flaky mobile
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sess_abc123" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rwx-1","prompt":"Write a short paragraph about sloths","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream > out1.log
# reconnect: pass resume_token from last-event, client appends the same request body
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sess_abc123" \
  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -d '{"model":"rwx-1","prompt":"Write a short paragraph about sloths","stream":true, "resume_token":"token:last_seq=14;gen_id=6"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream > out2.log
```

Sam (Customer): snippet of the SSE frames we captured:```

data: {"event":"token","seq":1}
data: {"event":"chunk","seq":10, "text":"...slow sloth..."}
data: {"event":"chunk","seq":14, "text":"...final sentence."}

# on reconnect we see the same chunks again:
data: {"event":"token","seq":1}
data: {"event":"chunk","seq":10, "text":"...slow sloth..."}
data: {"event":"chunk","seq":14, "text":"...final sentence."}
```

Maya (CSE): that helps. are you sending an idempotency key or unique request id per original request? also can you share the X-Redwood-Request-ID from headers in the responses?

Sam (Customer): we don't currently set a per-request idempotency key. I have one response header from first connection: `X-Redwood-Request-ID: rwd_20260314_7b9` and from the reconnect attempt: `X-Redwood-Request-ID: rwd_20260314_7b9` (same).

Joon (Infra): seeing same request id on reconnect is expected if client resends identical payload without new id. That can confuse server resume logic if resume_token isn't authoritative or if resume boundaries overlap. Two possibilities: (1) server resumed by replaying last unacked chunks, but client also reconsumed them; (2) server created a new generation with same request id and didn't dedupe because resume_token parsing failed.

Priya (eng-sre): can you share the server-side log lines for that request id? do you have any logs showing resume_token parsing? If not, Sam we'll need the raw HTTP traces (response headers + first 40 bytes of stream) so we can match on gen fingerprint.

Sam (Customer): pasted logs in channel + sent the HTTP trace to support email. key parts: server accepted resume_token, then a resumed session emitted `resumed=true` but then server emitted a full generation with `gen_id` that matched the original — looks like replay instead of resume.

Maya (CSE): OK — quick mitigation for you: set a client-side guard to ignore any incoming chunk with seq <= last_acked_seq on reconnect. That avoids double-appending already-processed tokens. Also add an idempotency header `Idempotency-Key: <uuid>` per user-initiated prompt so server can dedupe if it sees identical payload and key.

Sam (Customer): we can change client asap. worried about already-billed duplicates for customers. is Redwood able to credit/dismiss duplicates?

Priya (eng-sre): we'll open a billing ticket. if we confirm duplicates were produced by the service during replay we'll coordinate credits. For the technical fix: engineering needs to tighten resume logic to attach a stable generation fingerprint (hash of request body + model + model params + user id truncated) to the resume_token and to the produced events so the server can compare fingerprint and avoid re-emitting chunks if it determines they were previously committed.

Joon (Infra): actionable items for runtime:
- ensure resume_token encodes last_seq and generation_fingerprint (sha256 hex)
- when a reconnect arrives with resume_token, server should perform dup-detection: if fingerprint matches an existing completed generation, return a short 'resumed: already_completed' event and short-circuit streaming.
- add a server-side dedupe window keyed by (user_id, fingerprint) for ~10 minutes to avoid duplicate billing on immediate reconnects.

Maya (CSE): for support triage please confirm: (a) exact customer request ids (b) client sdk name+version (c) whether they used a custom retry/backoff. Sam can you paste those?

Sam (Customer): request ids: `rwd_20260314_7b9` (initial), `rwd_20260314_7b9` (reconnect). SDK: internal mobile wrapper v0.9.2, which does an immediate reconnect without jitter for mobile backgrounding.

Maya (CSE): v0.9.2 immediate reconnect is probably the trigger. ask them to add jitter/backoff or a small 200ms delay before reconnect to avoid hitting dedupe race with in-flight server processing. Also implement the seq-ack guard.

Priya (eng-sre): I'm creating an internal ticket and assigning to eng-runtime for a durable fix. DeployBot: create ticket in JIRA 'ENG-RT-xxxx' and set priority P2.

DeployBot: Created JIRA ENG-RT-2147: "streaming: strengthen resume idempotency & dedupe window" assigned to eng-runtime, priority P2. :white_check_mark:

Joon (Infra): quick patch idea: server can emit a `generation_fingerprint` field on every chunk in the short term so clients can detect duplicates and avoid storing/displaying repeated content. low-risk and backward compatible.

Maya (CSE): agreed. Sam, we'll push two fast changes: server emits fingerprint on chunks (no client change required to ignore), and support will run a billing review for potential credits. Can you confirm preferred contact and customer account id?

Sam (Customer): account id: acct_77-xyz. contact: sam@acme.co. pls keep me posted. Thanks everyone.

Priya (eng-sre): next steps summary:
- support: open billing review + hold any immediate credits until engineering confirms duplication source.
- eng-runtime: implement resume_token fingerprint + dedupe window (ENG-RT-2147).
- infra: add short-term chunk field `generation_fingerprint` and ensure it's present in SSE frames.
- customer: implement seq-ack guard + add Idempotency-Key and small reconnect jitter.

Maya (CSE): noted. will follow up after billing review. :thumbsup:

Sam (Customer): thanks — applying client changes now, will test and report results.

Priya (eng-sre): marking this thread for handoff to eng-runtime. tagging @Joon to take ownership of the patch.

Joon (Infra): taking ownership. I'll post a design note in eng-runtime channel and ETA in 2 business days.

Maya (CSE): thanks. closing loop here once ENG-RT-2147 lands.

Sam (Customer): :white_check_mark:
